lines: Welcome to Module Eight, Lesson One: observability for agents.
Watching an agent takes more than watching a server.
Picture HomeShield, an insurer whose agent helps customers file home claims.
One day, a simple claim takes nine seconds and still gets it wrong.

say.0: Picture Home Shield, an insurer whose agent helps customers file home claims.

lines: Old monitoring can only say the request was slow.
An agent trace says why: the planner chose the wrong tool twice, and retrieval came back empty.
So make every model call, tool call, retrieval, and handoff a span.
Each one records the model and prompt version, tokens, latency, and cost.
It also records the tool's name and arguments, the result, and retries.
Run and session IDs tie it all together.
Those arguments matter.
Without them, you can't tell a wrong tool from the right tool used badly.
Use OpenTelemetry, the open standard that NeMo Agent Toolkit emits natively.
Instrument once, and send the same spans to Phoenix, Langfuse, Datadog, or any backend.

lines: But full traces hold customer data.
Redact it before export, limit retention, and guard trace storage like your production database.
Next, pick the signals worth an alert.
Task success rate reflects user value, and tool errors belong per tool, not just in total.
Rising steps per task, or more runs hitting their budget cap, mean the agent is struggling.
More escalations mean lost capability, and falling groundedness warns of hallucination.
A spike in one guardrail can signal an attack.
And p95 latency and cost per resolved task are your two targets.

say.1: And P ninety-five latency and cost per resolved task are your two targets.

lines: Then capture feedback.
Thumbs are precise but rare, while rephrasing or giving up are quiet signals you get constantly.
Tie each signal to its trace ID and feed the data flywheel.
That's how monitoring becomes improvement.
HomeShield once tried a cheaper model to cut cost per token.
It failed more and took more steps, so each resolved claim cost more.

lines: On the exam, when asked what to optimise or report, choose cost per successfully resolved task.
Now read on to see what every span should carry.
